requirement: `habeas status` and the mdBook requirements index MUST generate their Definition/Evidence Markdown tables through the same renderer. That renderer MUST calculate column widths, align the columns, and display the same evidence-state labels in both outputs. Callers MAY select different definitions and supply different kind-labeled name cells so mdBook can link to detail pages.
rationale:
**Implementation**
- `src/markdown.rs` `render_evidence_table` is the single renderer. It computes each column width as the widest cell, floored at the header text. It left-pads the header, the `---` separator row and every data row with the same widths, so the `|` delimiters line up. It takes rows of `(name cell, &str label)`, so callers choose which definitions to list and what name cell to show.
- `habeas status` (`src/commands.rs`, `status_markdown_with_options`) selects its own definitions and builds name cells like `` `name` (kind) ``. It calls `render_evidence_table`, and the call site is marked `{impl}` for this requirement.
- The mdBook index (`src/index.rs`, `DetailPlan::populate`) builds linked name cells like ``[`name`](href) (kind)``. It calls the same `render_evidence_table`, also marked `{impl}`.
- Both callers take the label from `EvidenceState::label()` in `src/index.rs`, via `evidence.state().label()`. The evidence-state labels are therefore identical in both outputs.
- All code that does this work is marked `{impl}`: the renderer, both call sites, and the `status_markdown_with_options` header. The other behaviours in those functions (selection, FIXME summary, navigation) are covered by their own requirement markers. I found no unmarked code that implements part of this requirement.

**Tests**
- `index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters` in `src/index.rs` carries `{test}` for this requirement. It builds a book with five states: Valid, Determination false, Invalid (two cases) and Missing. It checks that each row has a linked name cell with the correct state label. It also checks that every table line has its `|` positions identical to the header's, which covers alignment.
- The status side is covered by `status_tables_align_each_column_to_its_widest_cell` in `tests/commands.rs`. That test is marked for `status_table_alignment`, not for this requirement. It checks alignment and widest-cell widths for `status` and `status --all`. Together with the index test, it exercises both callers of the one shared function.
- A single shared function plus these tests covers the interesting points. Minor weakness: the index test does not assert exact padding width, and the status test is not cited for this requirement. Because the renderer is one function, I judge this adequate.
